scope: 2026-11-08 through 2026-11-11 Agent/RSI/JEPA focused primary-source review; not an exhaustive all-paper claim
review_boundary: Implementation decisions cover independently executable low-cost components only. No model API, checkpoint, complete agent rollout, official benchmark run, or capability improvement has been executed by this review.

deduplication.result: None of the seven reviewed identities occur in those inputs. La-JEPA 2611.08156 already has window-only P2 selection and is not counted as a new paper.
deduplication.priority_boundary: No Google/Meta affiliation appears in the seven primary-source author blocks. AlphaProof Code is owned by the separate priority reviewer; this file does not close the Google/Meta sweep.

papers.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
reviewed_sections: 3.4 Revisiting Source Evidence at Test Time
papers.code_status: Public author repository verified; Apache-2.0. No code or weights copied.
papers.algorithm: Fixed training runs are linked to per-run compilations and at most three immutable insights each. The test agent initially sees insights and may explicitly descend to the original evidence; the source corpus remains read-only.
papers.component_scope: Immutable training-run/compilation/insight graph, exact source digests, validated navigation and read-only actor memory views; no LLM compiler or task-solving agent.

cost_assessment.basis: Section 4.1 and Appendix A: five benchmarks/eight suites, multiple memory methods and three trials using a high-reasoning DeepSeek-V4-Flash terminal agent, plus memory construction and up to 200 environment steps. Complete grid is long hosted-model rollout work, not a cheap corpus operation.

papers.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
papers.code_status: No author implementation repository linked in the fixed paper; exact-title search did not identify one.
papers.algorithm: Before persistent memory admission, compare temporary and original states on paired transfer, falsification and regression probes. Commit only if gain, failure-rate and regression-damage thresholds all pass; a failed hypothesis may undergo one precondition refinement.
papers.component_scope: Equations 7-9 empirical gate over explicit verifier records; no fake actor, automatically generated probes, proposer or claimed generalization guarantee.

cost_assessment.basis: Appendix C.7 Table 4 reports approximately 460,000 LLM calls and 703,000 verifier calls across groups, up to 32 CPU workers, with individual groups taking 12-39 hours. Hosted API inference is not local GPU training and its provider compute is not disclosed.

papers.title: Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution
papers.code_status: Paper promises a future GitHub release but provides no author repository URL; no release found by exact-title search.
papers.algorithm: Separate natural-language strategy from linked executable procedures. Propose localized skill/program patches and retain a patched bundle only after strict held-out validation improvement.
papers.component_scope: Content-addressed program patches, syntax validation, immutable skill-program pairing, and strict validation-only accept/rollback. No LLM proposer, generated-program execution or spreadsheet-agent result.

cost_assessment.basis: Appendix A.3: 131,072-token contexts; up to 50 ReAct iterations during evolution, ten steps with batch eight, three independent evolution runs per method, three large/API backbones and four benchmarks including 1,000 test examples on each TableQA task. Full grid would require long repeated model rollouts.

papers.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
papers.first_author_affiliation: Columbia University; work during Amazon internship
papers.code_status: No author ReTrace repository linked in the fixed paper. Public benchmark repositories are not the method implementation.
papers.algorithm: Extract reasoning-grounded conditions, typed arguments and their provenance; aggregate them into a cited decision-list IR and synthesize a workflow where code chooses the next step. Model use inside individual tools remains possible.
papers.component_scope: Typed decision-list IR interpreter with explicit input/result provenance, first-matching guard, completion and support citations; no LLM extraction/aggregation/synthesis or autonomous production actions.
papers.production_evidence: The paper reports 79 internal production procedures and aggregate platform logs; those private procedures are unavailable. Public tests use tau2 telecom and SOP-Bench, not actual user A/B traffic.

cost_assessment.basis: Appendices C/D/L: hosted Sonnet/Opus construction, repeated merges and 36 requested constructions per trace configuration, training-only repairs and multi-benchmark execution; the internal platform and 79 SOPs are private. The reported $2.32 public one-time construction estimate is not an enterprise cost or a claim that the cheap IR interpreter itself is expensive.

papers.title: ARE-bench: Benchmarking Agents' Research Ability in Real-World Researcher Sessions and Workspaces
papers.first_author_affiliation: Fudan University; Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory research intern
papers.affiliation_boundary: Paper front matter lists institutions collectively rather than mapping each author; the first author's own homepage supplies his current affiliation.
papers.code_status: Project site verified but offers contact-based evaluation, not a public code/data download. No official dataset integrated.
papers.algorithm: Preserve still-valid background requests and the actual workspace at a real session cut. Score a separate intent-grounded checklist using strict all-item instance success and per-task macro checklist success; the actor must not receive the private rubric.
papers.component_scope: Actor/evaluator payload separation, exact checklist denominator checks, macro CSR and strict ISR; no fabricated official task set or agent evaluations.

cost_assessment.basis: 75 real workspaces, seven frontier models and three rollouts imply 1,575 long environment runs, plus checklist judging. Appendix G uses E2B/RJob/Docker and task-specific timeouts; Section 4.5 reports provider costs per run. Public source does not provide a downloadable task release, so this review implements only the CPU scoring contract.

papers.title: RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval
papers.code_status: Author repository linked by the paper and verified. No weights or dataset downloaded.
papers.algorithm: A shared order-sensitive Vision Mamba encoder learns from four scan traversals. Adversarial hard half-splits use straight-through gradient-reversal weights; four twin-excluded neighbourhood distributions match a detached within-sensor consensus.
papers.component_scope: Exact scan-path permutations, adversarial split forward/backward and equations 8-9 relational consensus. No replacement Vim backbone, pretrained checkpoint, full CVA/predictor training or cross-sensor benchmark claim.

cost_assessment.basis: Section 4.2 trains 100 epochs at batch 290 with a 12-block encoder, six-layer predictor and four CVA blocks on three paired datasets; DSRSID alone has 56,000 training pairs. The reported experiment grid includes independent repetitions and retrained baselines on four V100s. Full multi-dataset comparisons are outside the single-GPU time budget; the independent tensor operators are cheap and will be validated separately.

papers.gpu_validation_boundary: All eight tiny-tensor mechanism checks passed on cuda:0 in every seed; no remote-sensing dataset, pretrained backbone or capability benchmark was executed.

papers.title: BioMem: Agentic Memory for Biomedical LLM Agents
papers.first_author_affiliation: University of Massachusetts Amherst / VA Bedford Healthcare
papers.code_status: No author code repository linked in the fixed paper or found by exact-title search.
papers.algorithm: HMRU unions existing dense and BM25 retrieval, reranks with a cross-encoder and builds task-conditioned evidence prompts. Its distinctive contribution is controlled biomedical retrieval/fidelity/use analysis rather than a new standalone retrieval primitive.
papers.reason: Do not duplicate the repository's existing hybrid-retrieval score hooks merely to add another generic component. This selection does not reject the paper's empirical biomedical contribution or claim a completed implementation.

cost_assessment.basis: Four 8B-30B open models, five memory configurations and six biomedical tasks plus long conversations, with multiple sensitivity grids; MIMIC resources require access authorization. Exact full runtime is undisclosed. Do not launch model probes or acquire clinical data to resolve that uncertainty.

shared_integrity_constraints: No gold answer, plan or private evaluation rubric is sent to an evaluated actor.
Synthetic diagnostics validate operators and protocols, not task-solving ability.
No component is an executable evolve capability mapping merely because it has a catalog entry.
Complete expensive studies are not reproduced and are review DONE; low-cost operator delivery is tracked separately.
No official source outage is filled by DeepXiv; unresolved release status stays explicit.
